answer: A trellis lets only one vine climb each strand; a tax-filing anchor lets one agent identity grow from each filed return: the agent proves with a redacted receipt, verified at the tax portal, that it holds a tax identifier with a current filing. Forging another identity means filing a fraudulent return, a crime far costlier than spinning up accounts, while an agent loose in the tundra of anonymous sign-ups has no anchor. The cap is one identity per taxpayer per year, but the zenith is modest: places without digital tax checks are excluded, and revocation is slow since filings refresh yearly.
